feature: The sync script, docs, and pressure tests all know about the sixth command
expected: Pressure tests describe the GitConverge scenarios.

The lane-split reference states how the guard reads command lines (PowerShell backtick, escaped program words, abbreviated rebase --exec, --shallow-file, Start-Process -WorkingDirectory, update-ref options, refs/HEADS) and the claim stored under a refused name.

contains: In PowerShell text a backtick escapes the next character
``g`it`` is `git`, ``git sw`itch`` is `git switch`, and ``gi`t`` is `gi` followed by a tab, which runs no git

a program word written with a backslash, a backtick or a caret that spells a program the guard knows once the escapes are removed (`g\it`, ``g`it``, `g^it`, also after `env` and the other wrappers) is read as that program
(also by the abbreviations `--ex` and `--exe`, with the value attached by `=` or separate; `--e` is ambiguous for git and runs nothing)
`-m <message>` and `-mMESSAGE` take a value (`-m -d` writes the message `-d` and deletes nothing)
A ref under `refs/heads/` names a branch whatever the letter case of `heads` (`refs/HEADS/x`, `refs/Heads/x`)
- Whether a line is read at all:
A line with neither is not read.
A claim file stored under a name that `plan` refuses (section 5: a path component ending in `.`, a space or `.claim`) stays readable and keeps allowing the creation of its own branch.
